newsitem.title: FRANCE: French firm buys Scherrer fashion house from Seibu.
newsitem.headline: French firm buys Scherrer fashion house from Seibu.

text.p: Japanese retail group Seibu has sold the Jean-Louis Scherrer fashion house to EK Finance, a French firm grouping designer clothing and shoe manufacturers, a spokeswoman for Scherrer said on Wednesday.
The spokeswoman declined to reveal the price.
Seibu first acquired a controlling stake in Scherrer in 1990 and had increased its control to 97 percent in recent years.
EK Finance, controlled by businessman Francois Barthes, includes the Emmanuelle Khanh and Jacques Fath fashion houses and Harel shoes.
It acquired the decades-old Jacques Fath house earlier this year from troubled state-banking giant Credit Lyonnais.
Barthes said at the time his goal was to buy troubled luxury firms and reorganise their structure to improve their finances.

The house of Scherrer, which produces haute couture and designer clothing, perfume and accessories, was racked by internal conflict in 1992 when Seibu and minority shareholder Hermes abruptly fired its founder and designer, Jean-Louis Scherrer.
It was the first ouster of its kind in fashion history.
Seibu and Hermes blamed the house's declining performance on Scherrer and accused him of devoting too much energy to Middle Eastern clients. Scherrer founded the house in 1962.
Frenchman Bernard Perris has designed the collection since Scherrer's departure.
